title: Melanoma
explanation: Melanoma is a type of skin cancer that develops from melanocytes, the cells responsible for producing skin pigment. It may develop in an existing mole or appear as a new, unusual pigmented spot. Early recognition and professional medical assessment are important. Visual appearance alone cannot confirm melanoma; diagnosis requires evaluation by a qualified medical professional and may require a skin biopsy.
observations: Asymmetry: One half of the spot may look different from the other half.
Border irregularity: The edges may appear uneven, notched, scalloped, or poorly defined.
Color variation: The lesion may contain multiple shades, including brown, black, tan, red, white, or blue.
Diameter: Melanomas are often larger than 6 mm when detected, but they can also be smaller.
Evolution: The spot may change in size, shape, color, elevation, or appearance over time.
Additional warning signs may include itching, tenderness, bleeding, or a sore that does not heal.
Some melanomas may appear beneath a fingernail or toenail, or on the palms or soles.
recommendations: Arrange an assessment with a qualified dermatologist as soon as possible if a new or changing suspicious spot is noticed.
Seek immediate help from a dermatologist.
Do not attempt to remove, scrape, or treat a suspicious lesion yourself.
Protect yourself from sunlight and avoid applying anything on the lesions
If appropriate, keep a dated photograph for comparison and share it with the healthcare professional.
Follow the dermatologist's advice regarding examination, dermoscopy, biopsy, or further testing.
medicalAttention: Prompt professional assessment is recommended for any new, changing, unusual, itchy, bleeding, or non-healing pigmented lesion. Do not wait for a lesion to become larger than 6 mm before seeking medical advice.
disclaimer: Do not try any medication or treatment on the lesion.
